question: On the pinned two-edge D4 path, what complete next-first public law follows one nonzero future red-X fault after action and postselection, and does the frozen five-round caller accept that stateful law?
role: One fixed-state exact physical-instrument discriminator plus independent read-only caller gate; not noisy production history, schedule performance or a general D4 density channel
program_alignment: Lab 005 physical-observation and fault-tolerance prerequisites: test whether future public charge depends on postselected history rather than only the current net red-X support before evaluating JIT schedules.
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 source red-X and ideal charge projectors

model.geometry_and_preparation: Periodic L=2, 108 physical qubits, pinned J6M common all-star/all-triangle +1 orbit; one private initial red-X support [0,4], no logical-sector assignment
model.ordered_timing: Prepare vacuum; apply private initial red X on [0,4]; measure complete eligible first 24-site binary flux/charge/vacuum record; take one public action defer [], partial [0], or matched [0,4]; if corrected measure complete eligible action-conditioned second public record; then apply exactly one new private physical red-X fault on edge 0; measure complete eligible next first record with no intervening correction or readout noise
model.private_state: Carry ordered first/second projector outcomes, initial red-X mask, correction mask and future-fault mask privately; the next projector is X_(E xor A xor F) A_s X_(E xor A xor F). Never replace the postselected state with a freshly prepared vacuum orbit after the action.
model.public_boundary: Only trial/prefix/action/future-key digests, public action IDs, and full 24-site binary flux/charge/vacuum arrays are decoder-visible; physical supports, projector operators, orbit and token are private. Defer has no second record.
model.matched_keys: One fixed trial ID; same private initial physical and first-observation keys for all actions; two enumerated second-exogenous bits for each correction; one fixed future-fault key and edge for every prefix. Keys are deterministic counterfactual labels, not Monte Carlo randomness.
model.independent_unit_and_uncertainty: One fixed exact vacuum orbit and geometry; all probabilities are exact rational Born masses, with no independent stochastic samples, confidence interval or bootstrap. Geometry and sector generalization remain unresolved.

matrix.full_public_next_first: At each positive pinned J6O prefix, check actual-sector flux/eligibility and commuting eligible projectors. Use exact ordered first/second/next-first Born contractions; classify every next eligible site's conditional charge, then enumerate the joint law over all non-deterministic sites, not a selected-site surrogate. Require exact normalization and 24-site public arrays.
matrix.counterfactual_discriminator: Compare defer+future-edge-0 with partial+no-future J7A after marginalizing partial second results at each matched first record. Both have the same final red-X support [4]. Record exact total variation of their complete next public charge laws; nonzero would show history dependence in this finite fixture, zero is a bounded negative result. This is not an isolated causal effect of correction because the measurement histories differ.
matrix.no_fault_control: Check that the J7A no-future limiting result remains pinned and unchanged; no-future probabilities are read from it, not recomputed or pooled with future-fault production rows.
matrix.caller_gate: Independently audit the pinned five-round history builder and evaluator: next first observations and hidden states are precomputed before action, and the evaluator uses the phenomenological second provider; report whether an action-bound private postselected-state/future-fault callback is accepted. Do not modify or invoke the frozen caller.

competing_explanations.current_support_only: After conditioning on the same final red-X support, the complete next-first law is unchanged by earlier postselection in this fixed fixture.
competing_explanations.history_sensitive_state: At the same final red-X support, the complete next-first law differs because earlier measurement/correction leaves a distinct postselected quantum state.
competing_explanations.censor: If a complete next-first law exceeds the frozen variable-site, term, row or CPU cap, retain only validated one-site diagnostics and make no support-versus-history claim.

acceptance: All six source/result/caller hashes pass before and after the matrix
All 10 positive pinned first/second prefixes preserve their exact J6O masses, and all three action branches close a normalized complete next-first law or are explicitly censored at a registered cap
Full 24-site flux/charge/vacuum public records are sector-correct; no private support or projector enters public output; exact replay and negative action/prefix/future-key checks pass

The matched-final-support discriminator reports exact rational total variation only if both complete laws exist; the independent caller gate reports integration status without changing the frozen caller
Zero stochastic histories, schedule arms, bootstrap replicates and new dependencies; no noisy JIT, general D4 kernel or threshold claim
stop_rule: Run source pins and caller audit, then the physical future-fault exact matrix at fixed edge/action grid. Fail closed on source, sector, commutation, normalization, public/private, binding or replay drift. Censor the affected physical branch at any frozen complexity cap; do not widen sites, change future edge, infer a numeric general kernel or start schedule sampling. A caller gap does not block independent exact fixture analysis.
